identity.title: An Observational Study for Grain Dynamics in the AS 209 Disk with Submillimeter Polarization

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present 870 $\ensuremath{\mu}m$ ALMA polarization observation toward the Class II protoplanetary disk around AS 209, which has concentric, multiple gaps and rings.

evidence.quote: AS 209 is a Classical T Tauri star in the Ophiuchus star forming region at a distance of 121 $\pm$ 2 pc (cite: gaia2018).
AS 209 is a Classical T Tauri star in the Ophiuchus star forming region at a distance of 121 $\pm$ 2 pc (cite: gaia2018).

question.value: What are the origins of the 870 um polarization in the AS 209 disk (self-scattering vs grain alignment), and what do they imply for grain size and grain dynamics?

evidence.quote: In this work, we perform 870 $\mu$m ALMA polarization observations of the disk around AS 209 and discuss the origins of the polarization.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA$\#$2017.1.00124.S.
The continuum polarization observations at 870 $\mu$m were carried out on 2018 May 16 during ALMA Cycle 5 operation.

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: four TDM spws centered at 336.5, 338.4, 348.5, 350 GHz

evidence.quote: Those four spws were centered at the central frequencies of 336.5, 338.4, 348.5 and 350 GHz.
The effective bandwidth of each spw is 1.875 GHz, providing the bandwidth of $\sim$7.5 GHz.
The antenna configurations were C43-2 with 43 antennas.
The beam size in the final product is 0.$''$94 $\times$ 0.$''$62 which corresponds to $\sim$114 $\times$ 75 au at the distance of 121 pc.
The total integration times for the target were 30.89 minutes in the observation.
The continuum polarization observations at 870 $\mu$m were carried out on 2018 May 16 during ALMA Cycle 5 operation.

what.value: Disk major axis PA 85.76 deg, minor axis PA -4.24 deg, inclination 34.88 deg

evidence.quote: We use the major axis position angle (PA) of 85.76$^\circ$ and minor axis PA of $-$4.24$^\circ$ with reference to (cite: guzman2018).
which is consistent with the previously obtained value, 577 $\pm$ 58 mJy within the uncertainty (cite: andrews2009).

method.value: Debiased PI from Stokes Q,U, PF=PI/I, angle theta=0.5 arctan(U/Q), with error propagation; keep >3 sigma_PI

evidence.quote: All of these values presented above are derived only where the detection is above the threshold 3$\sigma_{PI}$.
thus $\Delta\chi$ $\sim$ 2$^\circ$/$\sqrt{43}$ = 0.3$^\circ$ in this observation.

analysis_steps.goal: Compare angles with circular vs elliptical tangents and find systematic offset

method.value: Histograms of deviations with Gaussian fits; weighted mean and chi2 test at eight independent positions

evidence.quote: we select the eight positions in the outer region, where the contamination from the central emission likely weak.

results_numeric.quantity: Mean angular deviation from elliptical tangents

evidence.quote: weighted mean of $\Delta$$\theta_{ellipse}$ = $-$$4.5\ensuremath{^\circ}$ $\pm$ $1.6\ensuremath{^\circ}$
the polarization fractions are almost uniform at $\sim$0.20$\%$.
the typical polarization fraction in the outer region is likely $\sim$1.0%
tan($\Delta$$\theta_{ellipse}$) = 0.08 $\pm$ 0.03

findings_qualitative.value: Inner polarization parallel to minor axis, consistent with self-scattering; outer polarization near-azimuthal (elliptical) with offset of opposite sign to the helicity-alignment prediction for clockwise rotation.

evidence.quote: the directions of the observed angular deviations are opposite to what is predicted under the fact that the disk rotates clockwise.

claims.experiment: Compare angles with minor axis and measure PF
claims.result: Vectors along minor axis; PF ~0.2%, below the 2-3% expected for a_max~140 um
claims.finding: Self-scattering dominates; grain size distribution differs (a_max ~50 or ~400 um or two populations)

evidence.quote: Therefore, we conclude that self-scattering dominates the polarized emission in the inner region of the AS 209 disk at 0.87 mm.

claims.hypothesis: Outer polarization comes from mechanically aligned drifting grains
claims.finding: Mechanical alignment needed but the sign of the offset is inconsistent with the helicity model for clockwise rotation

evidence.quote: This poses a question in our understandings of the alignment processes and/or grain dynamics in protoplanetary disks.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Gold mechanism considered but requires St>~10 where emission is inefficient; grain diffusion gives the same pattern as accumulation

evidence.quote: it is uncertain whether the observed orientations can be explained by the possible grain dynamics.

limitations_admitted.value: Large beam limits angle analysis; beam dilution effects

evidence.quote: the large beam size effects are not negligible.

referee_caveats_inferred: Small sample (8 independent positions) and marginal S/N
Sign convention of angles could affect the key conclusion

reproducibility.score_reason: Short recipe with the key imaging parameters and formulas, but several calibration and selection details are missing.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Public data likely but the paper does not state it, and calibration details are missing.
